panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left panel shows palmar hands with purpuric papules/edema in a case captioned as typical PPGSS in a child; matches gloves distribution. in_text_mentions: munities after the first eruptions, laboratory findings, and epidemiology findings led us to suspect that several skin eruptions, namely Gianotti-Crosti syndrome (GCS, also known as papular acrodermatitis of childhood)1–3 (Figure 1), pityriasis rosea (PR)4–6 (Figure 2 and Figure 3), asymmetrical periflexural exanthem (APE, also known as unilateral latero-thoracic exanthem)7–9 (Figure 4), unilateral mediothoracic exanthem (UME, a variant of APE),10 eruptive pseudoangiomatosis (EP),11–13 and papular-purpuric gloves and socks syndrome (PPGSS),14–16 are related to viral infections17 (Figures 5–7).

in_text_mentions: the rash progressed, leading to his admission to the dermatology ward. Clinical examination revealed multiple pustules and erythematous‑purpuric patches on the glans penis, scrotum, and perianal region, as well as a moderately pruritic, confluent maculopapular and petechial eruption on the palms (Figure 1) and dorsal surfaces of the hands (Figure 2) and feet (Figure 3) extending beyond the wrists and ankles, forming a classic “gloves‑and‑socks” pattern. Additional petechial macules were noted on the groin (Figure 4), hips, and buttocks, creating a sharply demarcated bathing‑trunk distribution.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Dorsal hand photo shows gloves-distributed violaceous papules coalescing into plaques as captioned for PPGSS; disease-focused title and in-text match. B: Dorsal feet photo shows socks-distributed violaceous papules/plaques as captioned for PPGSS. C: Close-up fingertip photo shows petechiae on palmar fingertips as captioned, part of acral purpuric eruption of PPGSS hands.
panels.attribution_text: Singh et al. Papular purpuric gloves and socks syndrome in a patient with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection.. JAAD case reports 2021. doi:10.1016/j.jdcr.2021.08.019. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Papular purpuric gloves and socks-distributed eruption. Clinical images on presentation demonstrated violaceous papules coalescing into plaques on the dorsal aspects of the (A) hands and (B) feet. C, Some petechiae were noted on the palmar surface of the fingertips.
in_text_mentions: ital signs, Fitzpatrick V skin type, and violaceous smooth papules coalescing into plaques on the dorsal aspects of the hands and feet and to a lesser extent on the anterior aspect of the left thigh (Fig 1). Petechial macules on the fingertips and shins were also noted. There was no involvement of the mucosa, palms, or soles. A 3-mm punch biopsy obtained from a representative lesion on the left dorsal hand demonstrated focal epidermal spongiosis, papillary dermal edema with extravasated erythrocytes, and a lymphocytic perivascular infiltrate in the superficial dermis (Fig 2).
